subject: Layered price-match proposal and implementation handoff for OptixHealth
messages:
From: Eddie Chen <eddie@optixhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: OptixHealth Procurement <procurement@optixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing alignment request — CloudVector counteroffer

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency and cost examples look promising. Procurement just came back: CloudVector has provided a counteroffer that undercuts list price on our expected usage by ~22% for the first 12 months (they're offering a mix of upfront credits + steeper volume tiers).

Before we escalate to legal, can Redwood match their economics while getting us parity on SLA credits and audit access? Key asks from my side:
- A rough headline equivalent (USD/month) for our projected 12-month usage (we shared the numbers last call)
- Whether you can structure a blended credit + per-token discount (front-loaded credit helpful for Q4)
- Confirmation on SOC2 evidence and access to request logs for 90 days

I'm attaching our RFP (Optix-RFP-20260901.pdf). Would like to close this week if possible.

Best,
Eddie Chen
Sr. Director, AI Infra
OptixHealth

Attachment: Optix-RFP-20260901.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Eddie Chen <eddie@optixhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing alignment request — CloudVector counteroffer

Eddie — thanks for sending the RFP. Looping in Jordan and Karthik to propose a concrete structure; copying Monica for onboarding sequencing if we land this.

Quick clarifying notes from our side:
- We'll validate the usage profile you shared, but I understand the bulk is production token generation with occasional eval runs (~65/35 split).
- On audit logs: we can provide request-level traces and configurable retention; SOC2 evidence is standard (we'll provide the report and coordinate an evidence package).

Jordan / Karthik — can you draft a layered offer that mirrors the CloudVector mix (credit up front + tiered runtime discounts) but with a Redwood reliability and migration handoff (can include a 6-week expedited onboarding + 2 free professional services days)?

Eddie — can you confirm the exact 12-month volume bucket (tokens/month) again so we anchor numbers?

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Eddie Chen <eddie@optixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed layered structure (initial) for OptixHealth

Hi all — based on the RFP and the CloudVector example, here's a suggested structure we can put on the table. I'll include hard numbers once Mateo confirms the monthly token anchor, but this is the shape:

1) Up-front onboarding credit (one-time): $120k credit applied over first 3 months to offset Q4 spend — intended to match the front-loaded economics Optix was offered.
2) Tiered runtime discounts:
   - Tier A (0—2B tokens/mo): list price - 10%
   - Tier B (2B—6B tokens/mo): list price - 18%
   - Tier C (>6B tokens/mo): list price - 24%
   (Discounts kick in monthly based on realized usage; we can smooth for the first 2 billing cycles if they prefer predictability.)
3) SLA & credits: 99.9% uptime SLA with service credits up to 25% of monthly invoice for sustained regional outages; handoff clause to fallback model variant for transient capacity shortfalls.
4) Audit & evidence: SOC2 report delivery + 90-day request log export (S3 delivery) and an option for an on-site evidence review for enterprise customers (charged separately).
5) Migration package: 6-week priority onboarding, 2 PS days included, and a technical migration runbook (Karthik to own compatibility checklist + early validation tests).
6) Term and handshake: 12-month committed term to align to their ask. Renewal pricing to be discussed at Q4 check-in with a 60-day notice window.

Attachments: redwood-layered-offer-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with modeled TCO scenarios).

Notes / constraints from engineering: Karthik — we should confirm whether request-log exports will include unredacted token-level latencies or if we need to redact PII by default. Marissa — since this is somewhat concessive vs list price, recommend a conditional clause: credits are contingent on activation by a target go-live date (we propose Nov 1).

Eddie — if that shape looks reasonable, we'll send a formal quote and DocuSign link for an LOI.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Eddie Chen <eddie@optixhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: OptixHealth Procurement <procurement@optixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed layered structure (initial) for OptixHealth

Jordan / Mateo — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few immediate clarifications from procurement/legal:
- The upfront $120k credit is in the right ballpark; procurement wants that to be a dollar credit (applied against charges) and not a separate rebate. Fine.
- SLA credit semantics: procurement asks that credits apply per-incident (rather than aggregate) and that the SLA be measured at the account level (not per-region). Are you open to a hybrid: per-incident credits up to 25% but measured account-wide?
- Audit evidence: SOC2 is fine. For the request logs: we need token-level timestamps (latency) but redacted text content; is that exportable as a CSV with request_id, timestamp, latency_ms, model_variant?
- Term flexibility: Optix is open to 12 months but asks for an early-exit carveout if there is a sustained >10% degradation in 90-day average latency vs baseline (for up to 2 quarters) — essentially an operational performance escape hatch.

If you can send a revised LOI with the hybrid SLA measurement, the log export format, and the early-exit language, procurement can sign off quickly.

—Eddie

On Thu, Sep 03, 2026 at 09:18 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Eddie — quick note: we can produce the CSV you described. Karthik, can you confirm redaction feasibility?

Attachment: Optix-RFP-20260901.pdf (from earlier)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eddie Chen <eddie@optixhealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Finalized layered match offer and next steps — OptixHealth (DEAL-10482)

Eddie / OptixHealth team — thanks for the constructive back-and-forth. Per our internal approvals, please find the finalized LOI shape below (this will be the DocuSign package once you confirm OK):

1) Pricing & credits:
   - One-time onboarding credit: $120,000 (applied as invoice credit across first 3 billing cycles).
   - Tiered runtime discounts (applied monthly based on realized usage):
     * Tier A (0—2B tokens/mo): list - 10%
     * Tier B (2B—6B tokens/mo): list - 18%
     * Tier C (>6B tokens/mo): list - 24%
   - Smoothing option: first two billing cycles can be averaged to avoid month-to-month volatility on discounts.

2) SLA & credits:
   - 99.9% account-level uptime SLA. Credits applied per-incident up to 25% of impacted monthly invoice. Minor transient throttles excluded; sustained regional outages covered.
   - Early-exit provision: Optix may terminate without penalty if the 90-day rolling average latency for provisioned model variants degrades by >10% vs mutually agreed baseline for two consecutive quarters; this triggers a 60-day cure period before termination.

3) Audit & logs:
   - SOC2 Type II report delivery within 10 business days of LOI execution.
   - Request-log export: CSV format with columns {request_id, timestamp_utc, latency_ms, model_variant}. Payload text will be redacted by default; unredacted export available subject to standard DPA/controls. Delivery via S3 transfer.

4) Migration & timeline:
   - 6-week prioritized onboarding commencing within 10 business days of signed LOI.
   - Includes 2 PS days and one joint go-live validation sprint. Go-live target: Nov 1, 2026. Credits contingent on activation by Nov 1 (see clause).

5) Legal & commercial notes:
   - Credits and onboarding concessions are contingent on execution of the LOI and a 12-month committed term.
   - Renewal will be discussed in Q4; any pricing for renewals requires 60 days prior notice.

Next steps:
- Eddie: confirm acceptance of the LOI shape and the Nov 1 activation contingent.
- Mateo / Jordan: upon confirmation we'll send the DocuSign LOI and the modeled TCO workbook (redwood-layered-offer-v1.xlsx).
- Monica: please stand up an onboarding intro call template for Optix and hold the week of 2026-11-01 for the validation sprint.

If Optix signs this LOI, we'll route the final contract to legal with the approved carveouts. Hope this aligns — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through details.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/optix-DEAL-10482
Attachment: redwood-layered-offer-v1.xlsx (pricing model)
